rows: The West Texas Mesonet station south of Muleshoe recorded several severe wind gusts as thunderstorms moved over the area during the late evening hours of the 26th. A maximum wind gust of 77 MPH was measured at 20:00 CST. No damage was reported.
The Bailey County Sheriff's Office reported three-quarter inch size hail just west of Muleshoe along Farm to Market Road 1731.

Multiple reports of large hail that ranged in size from nickels to quarters were received from the Needmore vicinity just before 19:30 CST. The severe storm that impacted the Needmore area was a left-moving (anticyclonic) supercell. Although reports indicated that motorists along…
An apparent tornado crossed Farm to Market Road 1760, fifteen miles west of Muleshoe. Several utility lines and poles were damaged. Damage corresponds to an intense low level Doppler circulation.

Multiple structures in Enochs sustained damage as a line of severe thunderstorms characterized by a bow-shaped radar signature impacted the community. At least three structures with tin roofs sustained heavy wind damage. Road signs were blown down and a number of utility lines we…
Multiple reports of penny to quarter size hail just south of Muleshoe on Texas Highway 214. Hail accumulated on the driving surface.
Quarter to golf ball size hail reportedly covered the ground along a swath from the West Camp community southward along Farm to Market Road 1731.

Numerous law enforcement officials reported large hail that ranged in size from pennies to golf balls near Muleshoe between 18:48 and 19:36 CST. Initial reports indicated golf ball size hail northwest of the city along U.S. Highway 84. A police cruiser was damaged by the hail. By…
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Muleshoe recorded a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph. No damage was reported.
Law enforcement officials reported that tennis ball size hail fell in the community of Maple from an isolated severe thunderstorm over southern Bailey county. No significant damage was reported.
Local law enforcement officials reported nickel size hail in Needmore.
Storm chasers reported penny size hail north of Enochs along Texas Highway 214 near the Muleshoe Wildlife Refuge.

Multiple reports of large hail were received as a severe thunderstorm impacted a swath from near Maple to Muleshoe. A report of golf ball size hail near Maple was initially relayed by the broadcast media near Maple at 17:30 CST. By 17:33, penny size hail was reported in Muleshoe.…

Severe thunderstorm winds resulted in considerable damage in the Muleshoe vicinity between 17:35 and 17:45 CST on the 25th. Extensive damage occurred to a pair of trailer homes just southeast of the city, when one was rolled by the winds and a second home sustained heavy roof dam…
Local farmers reported hail up to three-quarters of an inch in diameter northwest of Maple. The hail resulted in no agricultural damage since crops were recently planted, and had not yet sprouted.

The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet recorded a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph just south of Muleshoe. These winds are believed to have been associated with the rear flank downdraft of an intense supercell thunderstorm which went on to produce giant sized damagin…

Emergency management officials reported that giant hail stones that ranged in size from baseballs to softballs resulted in significant damages throughout the city of Muleshoe around 20:00 CST. Numerous windshields were knocked out of vehicles and many structures sustained heavy r…
Local cotton gin operators reported that several hundred acres of young cotton plants were damaged by large hail south of Enochs.
An anemometer located at the Muleshoe Warren Airport recorded a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 65 mph at 15:00 CST. No damage was reported.
The public reported golfball size hail along Texas Highway 214 north of Needmore. No damage was reported.
A second severe storm impacted the Needmore vicinity and produced quarter size hail at 16:45 CST.
An evening thunderstorm impacted Muleshoe shortly after 19:00 CST. The Bailey County Emergency Manager reported nickel size hail in the city.

Local law enforcement and emergency management officials reported that large hail up to the size of quarters fell along U.S. Highway 84 from near Progress to Muleshoe. At 18:45 CST marble to quarter size hail was initially reported just northwest of Progress. By 19:01 CST, dime t…
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Muleshoe recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph. No damage was reported.
Emergency management officials reported that thunderstorm winds blew down utility lines and broke two inch diameter tree limbs along U.S. Highway 70 east of Muleshoe.

The convective complex and embedded high-precipitation supercell that impacted parts of Parmer County subsequently moved southward over Bailey County. A post storm survey by Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet meteorologists revealed a swath of intense wind damage from betwe…

A post storm survey by Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet meteorologists revealed that hail up to the size of nickels accompanied extreme thunderstorm winds in the Enochs vicinity. The wind-blown hail contributed to significant cotton losses.

Thunderstorms continued to enhance ambient winds immediately north of a passing cold front over portions of Bailey County. At 18:00 CST, the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Muleshoe recorded a 61 mph gust. No damage was reported.

A storm chaser reported half dollar size hail along U.S. Highway 84 in Bailey County. By 14:51 CST, the hail was intermittently mixed with very large 3.75 inch hail stones. No significant damages were reported.
Trained weather spotters reported very large hail of 3.75 inches in rural Bailey County. Minor damage was reported to vehicles along U.S. Highway 84.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph was recorded by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Muleshoe. No damage was reported.

The broadcast media relayed photographs of a non-mesocyclonic tornado which developed beneath a shallow convective cell between 12:40 CST and 12:44 CST on the 26th. Per post-event radar and surface analysis, the tornado occurred during the updraft phase of a small convective show…
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet station measured a wind gust to 60 mph 2SSW Muleshoe.
The public estimated golf ball size hail in Needmore at 1638 CST and a NWS employee reported half-dollar size hail four miles east of Needmore at 1644 CST. No damage was reported.
A NWS COOP observer estimated hail up to nickel size. No damage was observed.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe reported a wind gust to 60 mph.
Law enforcement personnel estimated quarter size hail on Farm-to-Market Road 1731 about one mile southwest of Muleshoe. No damage was reported.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site in Muleshoe sampled a 59 mph wind gust. In addition, numerous utility poles, power lines, and trees were reported downed near and south of town.

A strong low-level mesocyclone accompanied by destructive rear flank downdraft (RFD) winds tracked southeastward from Muleshoe to about 12 miles southeast of Muleshoe. Although law enforcement reported a tornado, no definitive evidence of such could be determined from the NWS sto…

Law enforcement personnel estimated hail of ping pong to golf ball size from Muleshoe to just south of the city. Strong to severe winds accompanying the hail enhanced the hail damage to roofs and sidings of homes, vehicles and windows.
Estimated by the Bailey County Sheriff's Office.
The Muleshoe Sheriff's Office estimated quarter size hail in the city. Damage was unknown.
A NWS CO-OP observer reported hail of 1.25 inches in diameter in Muleshoe. Damage was unknown.
Local media relayed a report of carport damage in Bula as severe downburst winds moved overhead.
Law enforcement estimated hail to 1.5 inches in diameter in Muleshoe. Damage was unknown.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
The Muleshoe Police Department and broadcast media reported hailstones up to golf ball size. Minor damage to some vehicles was noted.
Broadcast media relayed a report from the public of tennis ball size hail six miles south of Farwell, or about two miles west of West Camp in Bailey County. No damage was reported.
A farmer in Bailey County reported hail and wind damage north of Muleshoe.
A farmer in Bailey County reported hail and wind damage to his property north of Muleshoe. Several center pivot irrigation systems were knocked over. Also, a small shed was destroyed by high winds.
Storm chasers observed a very brief and narrow tornado over open land east of Enochs.
Copious amounts of hail up to golf ball size caused various degrees of damage to vehicles and roofing shingles, mainly across southern sections of Muleshoe.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured a wind gust to 72 mph at 2220 CST and then 82 mph at 2225 CST. Several windows were destroyed in a restaurant in Muleshoe.

Broadcast media relayed damage photos of a significant hailstorm that struck the community of Bula. Wind-driven hail as large as baseballs pummeled crops and caused extensive damage to siding, windows and roofs to dozens of buildings in the area.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
Storm chasers observed a landspout tornado for less than one minute in far northern Bailey County over open land. The tornado did not cause any damage, hence the EFU rating.
A cracked windshield and hail dents were noted to a storm chaser's vehicle.

NWS employees viewed a storm chaser's live stream of a very brief tornado. The funnel cloud extended 1/3 of the way down and kicked up a narrow debris cloud for less than 20 seconds. This tornado remained over open land and caused no damage.

Law enforcement initially reported a tornado near the town of Lariat. Broadcast media relayed a picture of a funnel cloud near the same time and location of the previous report. A NWS storm survey revealed that this tornado began in northern Bailey County along County Road 54 bet…
A storm chaser reported ping pong size hail south of Muleshoe on State Highway 214.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured a wind gust to 64 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured a wind gust to 72 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured severe wind gusts from 1735 to 1740 CST. A peak gust of 68 mph was measured at 1735 CST.
A storm chaser reported hail up to two inches in diameter about nine miles southwest of Muleshoe. No damage was reported.
Law enforcement in Muleshoe and an NWS cooperative weather observer reported quarter size hail in Muleshoe.
A storm chaser reported hail up to two inches in diameter in Needmore. No damage was reported.
A video received via twitter depicted hail up to two inches in diameter near the Muleshoe Wildlife Refuge. No damage was reported.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured a wind gust to 61 mph.

Numerous reports were received of a swath of hail from approximately three miles south of Muleshoe to the Parmer County line along Texas State Highway 214. The hail ranged in size from golf ball to tennis ball size. The hail swath continued into Parmer County. No damage was repor…
A storm chaser reported golf ball size hail in far southwestern Bailey County.
Several storm chasers reported a swath of hail between ping pong ball size and 2.25 inches in far southern Bailey County. No damage was reported.

A cyclic tornadic supercell produced several tornadoes over a period of approximately two hours. An NWS storm survey revealed that this supercell produced nine separate tornadoes. This tornado was the second tornado. The instantaneous width and center of the tornado was estimated…

A cyclic tornadic supercell produced several tornadoes over a period of approximately two hours. An NWS storm survey revealed that this supercell produced nine separate tornadoes. This tornado was the third tornado. While the larger tornado south of Enochs was occluding, a new ci…
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured severe wind gusts from 2105 CST through 2125 CST. A peak wind gust of 67 mph was measured at 2105 and 2110 CST.
Law enforcement in Muleshoe reported quarter size hail as an isolated thunderstorm moved over the city.
A member of the public reported ping pong ball size hail in rural western Bailey County.
Multiple storm chasers reported a swath of hail approximately seven to nine miles northwest of Needmore. Hail ranged in sizes from golf ball size to tennis ball size. No damage was reported.
Several storm chasers reported hail along Texas State Highway 214 south of Enochs. Reported hail ranged in size from half dollar to two inches in diameter. No damage was reported.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured severe wind gusts from 2143 CST through 2147 CST. A peak wind gust of 63 mph was measured at 2143 CST.
Severe downburst winds southeast of Muleshoe caused a train to derail.
Local broadcast media relayed a report of quarter size hail northeast of Needmore. Wind driven hail also damaged vinyl siding to a home.
An individual's personal weather station measured a wind gust of 66 mph northeast of Needmore.
A report on mPing indicated tennis ball size hail west of Needmore. No damage was reported.

Local broadcast media relayed a report and an NWS cooperative weather observer observed golf ball size hail in Muleshoe.
A public report was received of two inch size hail west of Sudan in Bailey County. No damage was reported.

Storm chasers and a hail research group reported hail along Farm to Market Road 596 south of Maple. Hail reports ranged between 2.90 inches and 3.10 inches in diameter. No damage was reported at the time.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured severe wind gusts from 0009 CST to 0010 CST. A peak wind gust of 65 mph was measured at 0009 CST.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe measured a severe wind gust of 58 mph.
